public_rationale: On the ordinary public-attribution reading, Palantir supplies a counterexample. Its August earnings call linked AIP to customer conversion and expansion while reporting 55% growth in realized US commercial revenue. Its filing establishes a hosted-software business and AIP's generative-AI component. This contradicts the central no-company assertion, but does not establish a separately measured generative-AI revenue contribution. The Microsoft parenthetical remains unscored.
limitations: The result depends on including vendors that sell both hosted and on-premises software.
The attribution is inferred from adjacent management statements about AIP-driven expansion and realized revenue.
A stricter requirement for separately quantified generative-AI revenue would leave this evidence insufficient.
The earnings call and filing were read through third-party reproductions.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Other than Microsoft, which has barely been able to sell it, he can find no public SaaS company that appears to have attributed any meaningful revenue growth to generative AI.

statement.excerpt: Other than Microsoft — which has barely been able to sell it as it is — I can find no public SaaS company that appears to have attributed any meaningful revenue growth to generative AI.

from_speaker: which has barely been able to sell it
I can find no public SaaS company
our_interpretation: Assess the public-record proposition, not what the author personally searched or knew.
An explicit company attribution of substantial realized revenue growth qualifies; a separately audited generative-AI revenue line is not required by appears to have attributed.
Bookings, contract values, forecasts and annualized run rates alone do not qualify.
Public SaaS companies includes publicly traded vendors selling hosted software subscriptions even if they also sell on-premises software and services.
Use April through June 2024 as the latest completed calendar quarter ordinarily reported before publication. Earnings commentary published afterward but before the post can describe that quarter.
The Microsoft parenthetical has no sales threshold and is assessed only as contextual qualification, not as a separately resolved quantitative proposition.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive review of contemporaneous public SaaS disclosures finds no qualifying attribution outside Microsoft, with apparent counterexamples shown to concern other metrics, other technologies or immaterial growth.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one qualifying public SaaS company other than Microsoft publicly links substantial realized revenue growth in the target period to its generative-AI offering.

evidence.excerpt: AIP driving both new customer conversions and existing customer expansions in the US.
evidence.locator: CFO Dave Glazer's prepared remarks, commercial segment discussion; immediately before the quarterly US commercial revenue sentence
evidence.publisher: Palantir earnings call, reproduced by Roic AI
evidence.explanation: In the same passage, management reported US commercial revenue of $159 million, up 55% year over year, and attributed customer conversion and expansion to AIP. Reading that passage as an attribution of meaningful revenue growth is an inference from management's explanation, not an independently measured AIP revenue allocation.

evidence.excerpt: continuous access to our hosted software throughout the contract term.
evidence.locator: Form 10-Q, Components of Results of Operations, Palantir Cloud; also Business Overview
evidence.explanation: The filing describes hosted software subscriptions and identifies AIP as combining existing platforms with generative models, including LLMs. It supports including Palantir in the stated company population, while showing that AIP is a combined offering rather than an isolated generative-AI revenue category.

evidence.excerpt: Copilot customers increased more than 60% quarter-over-quarter.
evidence.locator: Satya Nadella's prepared remarks, future of work discussion
evidence.explanation: Microsoft reported growing customer adoption, which qualifies the barely-selling characterization. Customer growth does not establish absolute sales scale or revenue, so it is not decisive for either the revenue claim or the undefined parenthetical.
